messages:
kevin: Heads up — tenant_id_type migration scheduled TOMORROW 02:00 UTC. Plan is CTAS -> swap -> backfill user_profiles.user_tier. Need owners for holdpoint at quiesce and canary. Release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/tenant-id-migration-2
rita: I can own the quiesce/holdpoint watch. What's our exclusive lock strategy?
eli: Suggest pin app to v2.14 (metric gating) for +4h post-cutover. App flag to read old column while backfill runs.
sara: Backfill job: profile_backfill_v2 running as batch worker, parallelism=8, expected ~3h for prod. Canary on 1% tenant first. Will post progress.
kevin: Good. Ops/DB - estimated lock time for CTAS & index create? If index needs exclusive lock longer than 30s we need a fallback.
rita: Quick check: CTAS should avoid long locks if we build indexes CONCURRENTLY where supported. For Postgres we'll do:
```sql
BEGIN;
CREATE TABLE user_profiles_v2 AS SELECT * FROM user_profiles WHERE false;
-- load via insert in chunks
COMMIT;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON user_profiles_v2 (tenant_id, created_at);
```
This limits exclusive locks to brief swaps.
deploy-bot: Migration job scheduled by release pipeline. Canaries: 1/100 tenants at 02:05 UTC, then ramp to 10% at 02:30 if metrics stable.
opsbot: Quiesce signal set for 01:55 UTC. Will post when traffic is drained below 200 req/s.
michael: FYI I ran the dry-run on staging, index create concurrent took ~12s for our sample size. Backfill chunking worked fine. Logs attached to the run.
rita: Adding holdpoint at 02:10 UTC for manual approval before final swap.
kevin: Approval gating: error rate <0.3%, p50 latency within 15% of baseline, and backfill progress >2%/10m on canary.
eli: Also add feature-flag toggle 'user_profile_v2' to switch reads to new column. Rollback = flip flag off + stop new writes. That's our safest reversal.
sara: I'll emit periodic progress in thread once backfill starts. Parallel workers will post every 10m.
deploy-bot: Holdpoint engaged at 02:10:00 UTC. Waiting for approval command: `/approve-migration 1749994321`
michael: `/approve-migration 1749994321` — approving to continue. Monitoring console open.
deploy-bot: Holdpoint cleared by michael at 02:12:07. Proceeding with final swap canary.
opsbot: Traffic quiesced at 01:58 UTC to 180 req/s for tenant sample.
rita: During canary: watch row-lock wait times. If avg wait > 50ms for 60s we abort.
sara: Canary started 02:05 UTC. Backfill progress: 1.4% complete. ETA ~3h10m.
kevin: If backfill slips past 4h, we trigger incremental resume mode: stop full-table writes to new column and resume in smaller batches, keep feature flag in place.
rita: Confirming rollback plan: DO NOT attempt full DB schema revert. Use app-level flag rollback + resume backfill later. DB restore only if catastrophic.
michael: Noted. I pushed a small compatibility shim to ensure old codepaths tolerate missing user_tier until backfill done.
sara: Canary progress 02:25 UTC — 4.2% complete, no errors, p50 latency +8%.
opsbot: Alert rule: if write error rate >0.5% for 2m, pause deploy. No alerts so far.
kevin: Keep eyes on replication lag during heavy chunks — no lag > 10s allowed.
sara: Backfill job log sample:
```
[02:32:10] worker-3: processed 12k rows (total 124k), avg_chunk=1.2s
[02:32:20] worker-7: processed 11.5k rows
```
kevin: Good. Plan to ramp to 10% at 02:30 if metrics stable. If anything fails, hit `/abort-migration` and we flip flag.
michael: I will be on-call for the 02:00 window and ready to execute `/abort-migration` if needed.
sara: 02:40 canary finished: 11.9% complete overall, no errors, p50 +7%. Ramping to 10% now.
deploy-bot: Canary ramp successful to 10% at 02:41:05 UTC. Continuing backfill.
rita: Manual checkpoint at 03:00 UTC — backfill 28% complete, CPU spikes transient but within limits.
kevin: If we hit any unexpected exclusive lock during index swap, fallback: pause writes to user_profile_v2 and run index create on a replica then promote. Documented in runbook.
opsbot: Quiesce released at 03:10 UTC. Traffic normalizing.
sara: 03:20 update — backfill 46% complete. Still on schedule.
michael: All good here. No rollback required.
sara: Final note: once backfill completes, we'll schedule the post-migration cleanup (drop old column after 7 days and run compact job). Will open follow-up.
kevin: Thanks team — great coordination. Closing thread and will file release notes summary in the release doc.
